question: Who survived to see the promised land during the Exodus?
summary: Numbers 14:22-24 has Yahweh swear that none of the rebellious generation will see the promised land 'but my servant Caleb' — singular. Numbers 14:37-38, 26:64-65, and 32:10-12 all explicitly include Joshua alongside Caleb as the two survivors. The first passage names only Caleb; the surrounding passages name both Caleb and Joshua.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the singular "but my servant Caleb" not as exclusive but as a partial naming, with Joshua excepted too and named in the very same chapter and the later musters.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, compiler of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the wording at face value: Numbers 14:24 swears that of the doomed generation only Caleb will see the land, yet the surrounding passages list Caleb and Joshua as the two survivors.

link.title: GotQuestions: Who was Caleb in the Bible?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment; presents Caleb and Joshua as the only two of their generation to survive and enter Canaan, citing Numbers 14:11-24 and the 'different spirit' that singles Caleb out.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Joshua was also excepted, but he is not named because he was no longer in the ranks of the people, being a constant attendant on Moses.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly states that Joshua was 'also excepted' and gives the contextual reason the oath at 14:24 names only Caleb — the core harmonization of singular-Caleb vs Caleb-and-Joshua.
excerpts.source_note_text:
my servant Caleb--Joshua was also excepted, but he is not named because he was no longer in the ranks of the people, being a constant attendant on Moses.
because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully--Under the influence of God's Spirit, Caleb was a man of bold, generous, heroic courage, above worldly anxieties and fears.
